sentences.text: Teleidosaurus was an extinct carnivorous marine crocodile relative whose name means "complete lizard" in Greek.
Jacques Amand Eudes-Deslongchamps named the type species in 1866, but his son Eugène Eudes-Deslongchamps established the genus name Teleidosaurus in 1869.
It is classified as a non-metriorhynchid metriorhynchoid because it mixes metriorhynchid skull features with ancestral thalattosuchian traits in its lower jaw.
Recent phylogenetic analyses suggest that the genus Teleidosaurus is not a monophyletic group.
The species T. joberti is a junior synonym of T. calvadosii, while T. bathonicus and T. gaudryi were reassigned to the genus Eoneustes.

Teleidosaurus lived during the late Bajocian to early Bathonian stages of the Middle Jurassic in Normandy, France, and is the most basal genus of marine crocodyliforms within the superfamily Metriorhynchoidea.
The time range for Teleidosaurus spans from the Bajocian to the Kimmeridgian, between 168.6 and 152.21 million years ago.
